[issue by Tkingoftheskies]
[crash-2026-07-11_13.50.55-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29927102/crash-2026-07-11_13.50.55-client.txt)

### Description

Latest Create Version on Neoforge for 1.21.1 - 6.0.10+mc1.21.1.

This bug continues to crash my server or singleplayer world every time i rejoin. 
I first came across this bug when i was on a server with others online but not in the area, when my game crashed they could continue playing, until i rejoined for the first time and it kicked everyone (including me) out with a "getsockopt" error. Now whenever anyone tries to join they get a "getsockopt" error regardless of whether i am also trying to join or not.

I connected 2 Large water wheels to a rotation speed controller (set to 256) and then connected that to a rope pulley with a drill on the end, i then changed the rotation direction - to make the pulley go down. I then added another rope pulley to the system - directly onto the already placed rope pulley - and it overstressed (as it should because the large water wheels provide 516 su each and the rope pulley (on 256 rpm) requires 1024 su, so just enough to power one rope pulley). I then lowered the rpm of the rotation speed controller to exactly 128 rpm and it crashed.
After some testing, i found that it only happens when you lower it from overstressed (>128) to exactly 128 (lowering it to anything other than 128 seems fine). If you lower it to <128 and then up to 128 it works as intended - does not crash and is not overstressed.


This example is on a creative world with some other mods that i used to replicate this bug
I have also recreated this with just the latest neoforge version and no other mods, the result is the same.
https://medal.tv/games/minecraft/clips/n5OvaY9UOSIWOSdOK?invite=cr-MSxleUcsNjgxMzY2NTA5

Hello!
We've been having a similar issue, specifically with Rotation Speed Controllers connected to Stationary Contraptions with Mechanical Drills on them. Twice on a previous server, and once in our current server. While the previous two crashes were a while ago and thus cannot find the Crash Log for, this third one we do have! Here it is: https://mclo.gs/0cwSOBn
It should be noted a consistent method to solve this issue is deleting the offending blocks/contraptions, often very easy to track down as it crashes immediately on activation or load. In our previous two cases, it was the Rotation Speed Controller. In this specific case, it was the stationary_contraption itself!
